feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear domain focus and solid progression at NACo. It reads professionally and shows scope well, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with more responsibility statements than outcome-driven achievements.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience consistently support a strong niche in digital platforms, governance, analytics, and public-sector communications.  
- Credibility and progression: long tenure at one organization with steady advancement from coordinator to director signals trust, growth, and leadership.  
- Good use of scale indicators: examples like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers” add impact and specificity.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope: include results such as traffic growth, engagement lifts, production savings, adoption rates, campaign performance, or operational efficiencies.  
- Reduce duplication across Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and project summaries; this would tighten structure and improve readability.  
- Minor style/consistency issues: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s” usage is fine, but punctuation in bullets is inconsistent; “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “A2 (learning)”; “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization may feel stylistically inconsistent unless intentional. No major misspellings or grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning with clear seniority and public-sector relevance. However, it overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent experience, and would be stronger with one or two concrete signals of scale.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and sharpen the opening: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing web, content, and analytics systems for high-volume public-sector organizations.”
- Add scale or scope from recent roles to increase impact, e.g., “Led a 10,000+ page Drupal migration supporting 3.5M annual page views and 50+ publishers.”
- Replace the generic “building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind” with more direct verbs like “leading,” “modernizing,” or “scaling.”
- Consider a cleaner second sentence: “Combines enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, editorial operations, multimedia, and AI-enabled search to improve how mission-driven organizations publish and serve users.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; “AI-enabled search” is more specific.
- “Enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production” repeats multiple skills sections almost verbatim.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be more effective if tightened into sharper, less repetitive capability areas with more consistent phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and simplify wording: “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “Enterprise website modernization.”
- Replace broad items with clearer capability labels: “Content governance and editorial systems,” “Analytics, dashboards, and reporting.”
- Combine overlapping ideas for tighter impact: “Workflow automation, integrations, and platform operations.”
- Suggested rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Content governance and editorial systems • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” repeats language from the header and Recent Projects.
- This section substantially overlaps with Topline Skills; consider using this block for broader themes and leaving tools/platforms to later sections.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding parallel structure will improve scanability and impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected Recent Projects” to reinforce recency; keep each item to one crisp outcome-focused line.
- Use consistent action verbs and style: “Led,” “Built,” “Developed,” “Produced”; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for consistency.
- Sharpen specificity where possible: e.g., “legislative search,” “Drupal 10 microsite,” “interactive conference display,” “website, email, and social.”
- Consider this tighter version:  
  **AI Hybrid Search** Led development of an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat.  
  **We Are Counties Microsite** Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, and downloadable resources.  
  **Organization Anniversary Campaign** Developed a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and a 10-by-20-foot interactive conference display.  
  **Advocacy Video Series** Produced a recurring advocacy video series spanning editorial planning, production, and distribution across web, email, and social.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search and Advocacy Video Series overlap with bullets in recent roles; keep footer more concise or frame as “Selected Projects.”
- “Modular structure designed for continued campaign growth” echoes broader platform/governance language elsewhere.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and NACo entries. Tighten it around distinctive consulting impact, platform delivery, and the AI search initiative.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + client type + value: “Embedded consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and communications systems modernization.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise”) with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Built,” “Led,” “Launched,” “Standardized,” “Improved.”
- Consolidate into 3–4 bullets focused on: enterprise workflows/analytics, Drupal campaign builds, cross-channel governance, and AI-enabled search.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages/users, publishing teams supported, toolkit downloads, search accuracy/lift, time saved, or campaign engagement.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, and enterprise web improvement” repeats themes already covered in the summary, competencies, and NACo roles.
- The Drupal microsite and AI search bullets may duplicate Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and reserve project specifics for the footer.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics; it should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles. Lead with transformation, team scope, and enterprise impact.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget strategy for a high-volume public-sector communications operation.”
- Rewrite the website bullet to foreground outcome: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel/video bullets more results-oriented: add growth, production volume, cost savings, turnaround time, or engagement gains if available.
- Tighten analytics/governance bullets: “Built reporting infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to improve leadership visibility and decision-making”; “Established governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning workflows to improve consistency and operational efficiency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-program language also appears in older NACo roles; emphasize building the in-house studio, scale, or strategic impact instead.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item is too close to the adjacent NACo roles and reads as operational support rather than clear leadership. Tighten it around scope, channel ownership, and outcomes to distinguish it from the later director role and earlier producer role.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper lead: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Combine and tighten bullets: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video bullet for ownership and impact: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Make workflow/editorial bullets more concrete: “Built stronger editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving publishing consistency and cross-team coordination.” Add metrics if possible: open rates, video views, publishing volume, turnaround time.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial coordination” overlap with the Director of Digital Media entry; avoid repeating governance language.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role, so emphasize expansion/standardization here, not creation.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent experience. It should be tighter, more distinctive, and aligned to the most senior/recent strengths.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, senior-level language tied to current positioning:  
  **• Enterprise digital strategy • Content governance and editorial operations • Cross-channel communications leadership • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Audience and journey-based content strategy**
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “communications” to sound more strategic and less tactical.
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; avoid mixing leadership, planning, and messaging styles.
- If space allows, emphasize modernization/operations over generic content planning, since that is better supported by recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” substantially duplicate the header and Core Competencies.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is weaker and less differentiated than the governance/operations language used elsewhere.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:

- WordPress
- SharePoint

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes, with only the most relevant tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”

- Use “enterprise CMS platforms” or “Drupal-led web platforms” to better reflect recent, higher-impact work in Drupal modernization and AI search.
- Keep this section concise; let the Technical + IT section carry the full software inventory.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search experiences” duplicates Core Competencies and recent project content; keep it here only if shortened elsewhere.
- Drupal/WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages already appear in Technical + IT.

Suggested edit:

Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value delivery capabilities tied to recent leadership work, not tool-level detail.

- Reframe from task list to capability/outcome language: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio system operation • Virtual event production workflows”

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Use it to signal depth and recency—especially Drupal—rather than repeat a bare tool list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize platform leadership, e.g. **CMS Platforms (Enterprise & Public-Sector)**.
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites, modular content)** • **WordPress** • **SharePoint** • **Power Pages** • **GitHub Pages**.
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of just names: **Drupal 10**, **enterprise publishing**, **campaign microsites**, **multi-author environments**.
- If no qualifiers are possible, consider trimming **GitHub Pages** unless it reflects meaningful recent work; it reads lighter than the others.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; differentiate this section with platform depth, not another repeated list.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid overloading other sections with the same unqualified keyword.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools you actively use in recent work and group items more clearly.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Front-end & implementation:** HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery; **Integrations & deployment:** API integrations, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions; **Tagging & tracking:** Google Tag Manager
- Drop version numbers unless they matter technically; “HTML” and “CSS” are cleaner than “HTML5/CSS3.”
- Consider replacing broad terms with stronger phrasing if accurate: “REST/API integrations,” “serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers),” “CI/CD automation (GitHub Actions).”
- If space allows elsewhere, tie one tool to impact in experience bullets instead of here, e.g., GTM for analytics deployment or Workers for lightweight web functionality.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills may partially overlap with GitHub Actions; keep the distinction technical vs. operational.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation, PM & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by strongest/relevant tools first: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp**
- If space allows, add light functional grouping for clarity: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/work management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If these tools were central in recent roles, consider replacing 1–2 names with outcome-oriented context elsewhere in experience bullets (e.g., “built Airtable- and Power Automate-based editorial workflows”).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; keep only if they support a broader systems/operations narrative.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful platforms to include, but this item is too bare and undersells a clear strength shown in recent roles: enterprise email operations and audience engagement. It should be tightened and framed to match the scale of your recent communications leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely relevance/enterprise weight: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope in brief parentheticals: **Higher Logic (newsletter/member communications)** • **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation)** • **Mailchimp (email campaigns)**
- If space allows, sharpen further with one qualifier: **Enterprise email, member communications, and campaign automation platforms**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” and NACo email bullets; keep this item platform-focused, not responsibility-focused.
- Avoid adding generic terms like “email strategy” here unless you remove similar wording elsewhere.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tool stack, but this item is currently a generic list and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In the Technical + IT section, it should read as a concise tools/methods inventory, with clearer grouping and less repetition.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI reporting/dashboard design**
- Replace **SEO** with **Google Search Console** or **SEO/performance analysis** to make it more concrete and tool-oriented.
- Replace **Dashboarding** with **KPI reporting/dashboard design** for stronger phrasing and clearer business value.
- Order by strongest/recent tools first; keep analytics platforms before methods.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This is nearly duplicated by **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider trimming one version or making this one strictly tool-based.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already substantiated in the 2022–2024 Director role, so avoid adding broad claims here that repeat that entry.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational: emphasize team-building, early platform/content ownership, and any scale or output metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving coordination across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete scope/results where possible: website refresh size/traffic, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience reach, email volume, or process improvements.
- Tighten the close to show leadership without overstating: “Produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”
- If metrics are unavailable, use sharper verbs: launched, streamlined, coordinated, produced, supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as the launch/early production phase.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; keep this version lighter and more execution-focused.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a notable “first podcast” achievement, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch and cross-functional project coordination, and trim generic references to digital content.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the clearest impact: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams.”
- Make the podcast launch the centerpiece: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a more specific support function, e.g., “Produced multimedia and digital content to support program communications and research dissemination.”
- If possible, add scope or output metrics: number of episodes, audiences served, teams supported, or types of projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item focused on innovation/research coordination plus the podcast launch.
- Avoid overstating digital leadership here, since stronger leadership evidence appears in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
